title: Internet and Telephone Support for Discontinuing Long-Term Antidepressants: The REDUCE Cluster Randomized Trial
authors: Kendrick T, Stuart B, Bowers H, Haji Sadeghi M, Page H, Dowrick C, et al.
population: Adults in 131 UK family practices taking antidepressants for more than 1 year for a first episode of depression or more than 2 years for recurrent depression, well enough to consider stopping and at low risk of relapse (PHQ-9 below 12, GAD-7 below 10); 178 in intervention and 147 in control practices; 4.9% of 6725 invited patients enrolled
funder: This study was funded by the NIHR Programme Grants for Applied Health Research (PGfAR) programme, grant reference RP-PG-1214-20004. The funder had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, interpretation, and analysis of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
result: Internet modules and telephone support from psychological wellbeing practitioners, with practitioner guidance including hyperbolic tapering schedules, against usual care. PHQ-9 at 6 months 4.0 against 5.0 (adjusted difference -1.1, 95% CI -2.1 to -0.1), noninferior. Discontinuation at 6 months 66 of 145 (45.5%) against 54 of 129 (41.9%), adjusted OR 1.02 (0.52 to 1.99). DESS withdrawal scores over 6 months lower with support (difference -1.6, -2.9 to -0.3).
